chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz al-Kūfī narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb al-Zayyāt, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Faḍl ibn ‘Abd al-Malik – or from a man from al-Faḍl, from Abī Basīr, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, the visitor of al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him) is the visitor of the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali, the third Shia Imam
key_terms.زَائِر: Visitor or pilgrim (one who performs ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting Imam Husain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the theological concept of *ittisal* (connection) between the Imams and the Prophet, affirming that visiting Imam al-Husayn is spiritually equivalent to visiting the Messenger of Allah. It reflects the Shia belief in the continuity of prophetic authority, where the Imam serves as the living embodiment of the Prophet's legacy, making his visitation a direct act of devotion to the source of revelation.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz Al-Kūfi narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb Al-Zayyāt, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Faďl ibn ‘Abdil Malik – or from someone from Faďl, from Abī Basīr, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Verily the Zā`ir of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) is the Zā`ir of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).
